Faculty Seminar: Hanjin Lee Ethics in Mathematics: how to teach it at Christian Universities? As AI advances, the social practice of mathematics faces new ethical challenges. While more math and statistics students are entering the Big Data and AI sectors, they receive little ethical guidance in their formal education. Compared to the established professional ethics courses in engineering and science, mathematics and statistics departments lack similar curricula. This talk explores the ethical dimensions of mathematics and recent scholarly proposals. I will also propose a course design for ethics in mathematics based on a Christian narrative ethics framework.

Stat 245: Jim VanderMey Making the Invisible Visible: Ethics, Systems, and the Future We’re Building In a world increasingly shaped by data, design, and automation, the deepest ethical decisions are often the ones we never see — embedded in architecture, algorithms, and assumptions. In this keynote, Jim VanderMey draws on decades of real-world practice as a technologist and his formation in theology to explore how we can surface these hidden choices, provide ethical leadership in a pluralistic society, and anticipate the long-term consequences of what we build — before they are felt.

title: Handong U / Calvin U exchange
text:
This site has some information related to a 2026 faculty exchange between Handong University in Pohang, South Korea and Calvin University in Grand Rapids, MI.

Itinerary for Feb 13 - 22 when Hanjin Lee and Joseph Cho will be visiting Calvin University.

title: About
text: About this site

title: Possible Talks
text: Here are some talk ideas for our visit to Handong University. We don’t entirely understand the audiences at the different sessions, so we are you hoping you can help us select what would be most interesting/relevant for each audience.

title: Possible Talks
text:
Friday: Good Teachers Workshop

Inclusion and belonging in STEM classrooms (joint)

This is perhaps more broadly interesting than the next one, but we admit that the situation in the US is probably not the same as in Korea.

Integrated Ethics Labs (joint)

This would be more targeted towards those interested in ethics in Stat/DS/CS.

title: Possible Talks
text:
Tuesday: Faculty

Random Thoughts (Randy)

Based on a paper entitled Randomness and God’s Governance
could possibly be moved to the student colloquium

Let’s Talk Ethics (Randy)

This talk will reflect on some experiences in my classes and among colleagues related to including ethics in what we do and teach. What makes this challenging? What makes it rewarding? What resources exist to help us?

One of the topics listed for Friday
How and why to build community in a statistics classroom (Stacy)
Less Volume, More Creativity: Using R in Undergraduate courses (Randy)

How this principle led to the development of R packages like mosaic and ggformula and how it can/should guide the use of R (or other software) in courses.
perhaps too niche

title: Possible Talks
text:
Tuesday: Students

options for mathematics talks (Randy)

Calculus the Way it Might Have Been: An Introduction to Analysis with Infinitesimals
Domino Arithmetic (An introduction to generating functions)

options for statistics/data talks (Stacy)

Data for good? Experiences and principles of data consulting as service (Stacy)
Virtues and cautionary tales for the data analyst (who wishes to prevent technical mistakes that turn results to lies) (Stacy)

some fun examples of understandable small technical mistakes that can lead to massively wrong conclusions, and maybe how to avoid by humility, teamwork, judgment and attention to detail


Random Thoughts (see above)

Christian Foundation

Is the track record of the church and ethics a good one? Should we trust communities of Christians to do this well?

title: Thoughts on Ethics in Mathematics
text:
Case Studies

Are there any case studies that are about mathematics and not applications of mathematics?
Example: Lottery, insurance, casino – mathematics basically the same (risk, expected value, probability), but reasonable people might conclude different things about participation/legality of these.
Sally Clark Case (Murder, misuse of conditional probability)

title: Thoughts on Ethics in Mathematics
section: What sort of Math/Ethics mix are we looking for?
text:
What sort of Math/Ethics mix are we looking for?

Ethics of mathematics as a discipline?
Ethics of mathematicians as humans doing mathematics?
Ethics of applications of mathematics?

What if equivalent mathematics can be applied in more than one way?
